meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You entered a zero on Owen's essay before anyone called me, Hale, and he found out on his phone in the middle of class. I have twenty minutes. Who decided, and on what basis?
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.
You don't have time. Then the principal will make time, and I'll be in that office before I leave this building. Last chance, Hale: on what basis?
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.

I'm writing down October 15. Show me both, the outline and the line you say isn't in Hamlet, on paper, now. And students change their argument between an outline and a final draft, Hale; that's called revising.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that I see the October 15 outline and the line you say is not in Hamlet in writing, and that nothing about this goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, with nothing agreed.
What moved her: the dated October 15 outline, enough for small ground but no change of position.
